steps.name: Sample QC, count-type check, and confounding diagnostics
caveats: If the matrix looks TPM/length-corrected, do NOT hand it to DESeq2 as raw counts; flag it for the fallback in T1S2 instead.
If any metadata value (sex or age) is missing for any sample, report it — NA covariates will drop the sample from the DESeq2 model matrix silently.
The 13th column of counts.csv may be a name/ID column or an extra annotation column; inspect the header before assuming which columns are the 12 samples.
steps.context: Inputs: /eval-four-models-v2-without-covariates-n6-s1-1/data/inputs/counts/counts.csv (12000 gene rows x 13 columns; expected 12 sample columns + 1 ID column) and /eval-four-models-v2-without-covariates-n6-s1-1/data/inputs/metadata/metadata.csv (12 samples x 4: sample ID, condition, sex F/M, age in years). Single batch; no batch covariate needed. The data profile does not state whether Salmon length correction was applied, so the count type must be established before DE modeling.
steps.question: Are the 12 adipose samples (6 treated vs 6 control, with sex and age recorded) suitable for a ~ sex + age + condition model: do the 12000 Salmon gene rows behave as raw counts, do sample IDs join 1:1 to metadata, is any covariate confounded with condition, and are there sample-level outliers?
constraints: Inspect the counts.csv header before transposing to identify the ID column and the 12 sample columns.

Join sample columns to metadata rows on the sample ID and require exact 1:1 coverage of all 12 samples; fail loudly (non-zero exit, clear message) on any mismatch instead of silently dropping samples.
Determine the gene row ID namespace (HGNC symbol, Entrez, or Ensembl) from the ID column and record it explicitly for downstream symbol mapping.

Classify the count type: if values are integer-like with per-sample totals on the order of 1e7, classify as raw counts; if values are non-integer or each sample column sums to a common scale (TPM-like), classify as normalized input.
Report per sample: total counts, median expression, condition, sex, age; report per-group age min/mean/max for treated and control, and the condition x sex contingency table.
Build the model matrix for design ~ sex + age + condition and report its numeric rank; state explicitly whether any covariate is collinear with condition.
Produce PCA of variance-stabilized counts: PC1 vs PC2 colored by condition, and a second panel by sex; flag any sample that is an obvious outlier on PC1.
Use only locally installed R packages; no network access is available.
acceptance_criteria: A QC report (CSV tables + figure) containing per-sample statistics, per-group age ranges, the condition x sex table, the count-type determination (raw counts vs normalized), the model-matrix rank statement, and a PCA plot.
An explicit GO/STOP statement for the DE step: raw counts -> proceed with DESeq2; rank deficiency -> name the confounded covariate; normalized input -> use the voom fallback.

steps.name: DE treated vs control adjusted for sex and age
caveats: With only 8 residual degrees of freedom, do not add any extra manual low-count filtering beyond DESeq2's default independentFiltering — n=12 is too small to afford additional gene loss.
If T1S1 found sex perfectly confounded with condition (e.g., all males in one arm), the sex effect is not estimable: report this as a design limitation and do not silently drop sex without saying so.
Report the dispersion estimates in the output summary; flag genes with unstable dispersion if DESeq2 reports shrinkage warnings.
steps.context: Primary model per the research question: DESeq2 with design ~ sex + age + condition, where condition (treated vs control) is the coefficient of interest. sex is a two-level factor (F/M), age is continuous in years. Groups are unpaired (6 vs 6), so residual df after 4 model parameters is 8 — adequate but not generous, which is why the unadjusted sensitivity run below is required. LFCs are shrunk with apeglm for ranking; multiple testing is Benjamini-Hochberg.
steps.question: Which of the 12000 genes differ in expression between the treated and control adipose groups after adjusting for sex and age, and how much do the conclusions change when the covariates are removed?
constraints: Follow the T1S1 determination: if raw counts, build the DESeqDataSet with DESeqDataSetFromMatrix using design ~ sex + age + condition, with condition factorized so control is the reference level. If T1S1 classified the input as normalized, run limma-voom with the same design on appropriately transformed values and label every output 'derived from normalized input'.
Verify model-matrix rank before fitting; if rank-deficient because a covariate is confounded with condition, drop that covariate, refit, and document exactly which covariate was dropped and why.
Extract the condition coefficient; shrink log2 fold changes with the apeglm prior; apply Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment to the p-values.
Write the full ranked results table for all 12000 genes with: gene ID, best-effort mapped symbol, baseMean, log2FoldChange, lfcSE, stat, pvalue, padj, and apeglm-shrunk LFC.

Report the primary DE list as padj < 0.05, plus the subset of that list with |shrunk LFC| >= 0.58 (about 1.4-fold) as the meaningful-effect subset. If the padj < 0.05 list is empty, say so explicitly and provide the top 50 genes by padj clearly labeled as an exploratory, non-significant list.
Produce a volcano plot (shrunk log2FC vs -log10 padj, top hits labeled) and an MA plot.

Sensitivity: refit the same condition contrast with the unadjusted design ~ condition; report the Spearman correlation of log2FCs between the adjusted and unadjusted models, the overlap of the two padj < 0.05 sets, and the number of genes whose significance status flipped; state plainly whether sex/age adjustment materially changed the result.
If the treated and control age ranges do not overlap, report that and add the interpretation caveat that the age adjustment is partly extrapolatory.
acceptance_criteria: A full-gene ranked DE table with BH FDR and apeglm-shrunk LFCs for all 12000 genes, a volcano plot, an MA plot, the primary DE list with the threshold stated, and the unadjusted-model sensitivity comparison.
A documented decision on any rank deficiency or dropped covariate.

steps.name: Pathway enrichment of treatment-responsive genes
caveats: fgsea requires a rank list without NA scores and without duplicate gene names; deduplicate after symbol mapping (one symbol per Ensembl/Entrez ID) and report the number of duplicates collapsed.
GO term enrichment on an unpaired 6-vs-6 contrast is hypothesis-generating only; do not present individual GO terms as independent mechanistic findings.
Set names in the GMT files (HALLMARK_*, GOBP_*) must be kept intact in the output tables; do not strip prefixes.
steps.context: Input is the T1S2 ranked DE table (all 12000 genes with shrunk LFC and padj) plus the T1S1 ID-namespace determination. Locally staged human gene-set collections (all HGNC symbols, all offline): MSigDB Hallmark (50 sets, msigdb-hallmark-human, v2026.1) and MSigDB GO biological process / cellular component / molecular function (msigdb-go-human, v2026.1); WikiPathways human GMT is also staged as a secondary pathway resource. The count row IDs may be Ensembl or Entrez, so a symbol mapping step against org.Hs.eg.db (with the local UniProt human ID mapping as fallback) is required before any set testing.
steps.question: Which human pathways and biological processes are enriched among the genes that differ between treated and control adipose (adjusted for sex and age)?
constraints: Map count row IDs to HGNC symbols using org.Hs.eg.db according to the ID namespace determined in T1S1 (Ensembl -> ENTREZ or SYMBOL via the org db, Entrez -> SYMBOL; use the local UniProt human ID mapping as fallback where org.Hs.eg.db is silent). Report how many of the 12000 genes mapped and how many were excluded; use only mapped genes for set testing.

Run fgsea on the full ranked list (score = apeglm-shrunk log2FC, ties broken by pvalue) against the Hallmark collection and the GO biological-process collection. Drop genes with NA or zero-variance scores from the ranked list and report how many were dropped.

Run over-representation analysis (hypergeometric test) of the primary DE set (padj < 0.05 per T1S2) against GO biological process, with all mapped genes in the dataset as the background universe. If the DE set has fewer than 10 genes, use the top 100 by padj and label the analysis as exploratory.

Report the top 20 sets per tested collection: set name, NES or fold enrichment, pvalue, padj, and up/down overlap with the DE set; produce bar/dot plots. For GO results, note the nested hierarchy so correlated hits are not counted as independent findings.

Use only locally staged reference files; no network access. If a referenced collection is absent at run time, report its absence and continue with the remaining collections — enrichment failure must not block or invalidate the DE results.
acceptance_criteria: Enrichment result tables and plots for Hallmark and GO (fgsea on the ranked list; ORA on the DE set), or an explicit per-collection statement of why a collection could not be run.
A symbol-mapping report with the mapped/unmapped counts and the method used.

plan.title: Adipose treated vs control DE with sex/age adjustment
plan.analytical_narrative: Bulk RNA-seq on 12 human adipose samples (6 treated vs 6 control, unpaired) with Salmon gene-level counts (12000 genes x 12 samples) and per-sample condition/sex/age in metadata. The groups are unpaired and not age-matched, so the central design decision is modeling condition alongside sex and age (~ sex + age + condition) rather than a naive two-group test. First, diagnostics establish that the delivered Salmon matrix is raw count data (the profile does not state whether length correction was applied), that sample IDs join 1:1 to metadata, and that no covariate is confounded with condition. Second, DESeq2 with apeglm-shrunken LFCs and BH FDR answers which genes differ, with an unadjusted-model sensitivity run to show how much the covariates moved the result. Third, the ranked DE list is tested against locally staged human gene sets (MSigDB Hallmark, MSigDB GO) so the gene list is interpreted at pathway level. All references are local; no network is used.
